ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, it is known that the line $y=kx+b$ passes through points $A\left(6, 0\right)$ and $B\left(2, 2\right)$. If the line $y=x-3$ intersects with line $AB$ at point $C$, find the coordinates of point $C$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Given the problem, if the line $y=x-3$ intersects with line $AB$ at point $C$,\\
then we have the system of equations $\left\{\begin{array}{l}y=-\frac{1}{2}x+3 \\ y=x-3\end{array}\right.$, solving this gives $\left\{\begin{array}{l}x=4\\ y=1\end{array}\right.$\\
$\therefore$ The coordinates of point $C$ are $\boxed{(4, 1)}$.

claims.claim: Solving the system of equations y=-1/2 x+3 and y=x-3 gives the coordinates of intersection point C as (4,1).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: So solve the system of equations y=-1/2 x+3 and y=x-3. Let -1/2 x+3=x-3, obtaining 6=3/2 x, therefore x=4. Substituting into y=x-3 gives y=1. Therefore the coordinates of C are (4,1)
